key_facts: This document sets out procedural rules for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix, 30 October – 1 November, issued by the Race Director on 1 November 2026.

Drivers who exceed the maximum time between the Second and First Safety Car Line during qualifying laps, in-laps, out-laps or reconnaissance laps may be deemed to be going unnecessarily slowly and investigated.
Drivers who are caught by a faster car must allow it past at the first available opportunity; blue light panels will be shown when the faster car is within 1.2 seconds.
The rules govern parc fermé access, marshalling system operation, pit lane procedures, practice starts, track limits at specific turns, and Safety Car deployment and withdrawal procedures.
plain_explanation:
This is a Competition Notes document issued by the FIA Formula 1 Race Director for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix. It sets out the practical procedures and rules that teams, drivers and officials must follow at this event.

The document covers speed during qualifying and practice sessions. Drivers must not go unnecessarily slowly between the Second and First Safety Car Lines during qualifying laps, in-laps, out-laps, or reconnaissance laps. The maximum time allowed is set after the Second Practice Session. If a driver exceeds this time, they may be investigated after the session.

The document requires drivers who are caught by a faster car to let them past at the first available opportunity. The marshalling system will give a pre-warning when the faster car is within 3.0 seconds, using blue light panels, blue cockpit lights and timing monitor messages when the gap is down to 1.2 seconds.

Several sections cover pit lane procedures. The document specifies where team personnel may access the parc fermé area (the secure area where cars are held after qualifying and the race), how the marshalling system works when cars enter and leave the pit lane, and how practice starts must be conducted in designated areas.

Track limits are defined at specific turns. Turn 4: if a driver misses the apex and crosses a yellow line with all four wheels, they must rejoin using an asphalt route at Turn 5. Turn 11: if a car passes completely behind the red and white kerb at the apex, it must rejoin keeping to the right of one polystyrene block arrangement and then to the left of a second one. Turn 17: failures to negotiate this turn properly may result in that lap time and the immediately following lap time being invalidated.

The document also sets out how the Safety Car is deployed and withdrawn. Waved yellow flags and SC boards will not be used; instead, messages will be sent to all competitors and trackside light panels will display SC. When the Safety Car lights are extinguished, a green light panel will display and other trackside panels will clear.
